questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Germany as my study destination because I wanted to challenge my german language skills and the university had some great options within my study field.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy because the university had a To do list upon arrival and also an online introduction meeting. Generally I received all the information I needed on email. My Erasmus coordinator was also very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got help from the international office and my Erasmus coordinator.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found a dorm really close to campus, so pretty much on campus. The university referred to their website where it was easy to sign up.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Try to find housing close to campus since it is a little outside the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I received a guide on how to register. It took some time because there was a lot of paper work, but my host university was helpful over email when I had problems.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an online guide and two introduction meetings.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I could register after I got my login to my host university. It is important to notice the deadline for registering, which I missed. So it was a bit problematic to register because of fully booked courses, but you need to write emails to your teachers to register and then they will help you.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it in good time and before the courses are booked.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The options for master students are not a lot, so I had to pick BA courses. This is okay as long as your home university accepts it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is more flexible. There were also more group projects and presentations compared to UCPH. If you choose seminars you do not have an exam like at UCPH but instead you need to participate and do small papers, projects and presentations. You only have an exam when you choose lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my seminars in Let's talk about sex, Colonial legacies in health and healthcare in Africa, Global Health Inequitiesand Interkulturelles Training-Basis/Intercultural Training - basis (engl.) because they were different from the courses I have had at UCPH and the teachers were very good.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There is a fee from the university but you can get it covered if you apply for grants. It covers all public transport and it you get free access to museums and libraries. It is around 2000 DKK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and books were cheaper than expected and housing was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I joined sport activities like crossfit and yoga. The university had great sport options for very student friendly prices. The university had an Erasmus tutor group which arranged many activities for Erasmus students and they were really great. It made it easy to get friends.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the activities at you student dorm or look for cultural events at posters or on facebook. Bremen have many festivals, concerts, bars and markets where you can go with friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit other german cities with train, which is free because you get your student ticket.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture is not very different, so it was easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The german students are very friendly and helpful, so if you join a student festival or a sport club, they will invite you to events or to lunch.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I did appreciate the festivals and chilling by the sea.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not stress about all the paper work - everything will be fine as long as you hold your deadlines. 
Explore the city together with friends and alone. 
Join the Erasmus activities

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find your housing in good time

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus community and the social life in my dorm was great.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was to be away from a known environment and to learn to enjoy the small things and to enjoy my own company.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
